baselines: pair envelope as non-deployable upper bound
benchmark_subset: TRAIN/D1 only; no DEV, FINAL, TEST, Wulver jobs, new simulations, or oracle labels
candidate_family: one predeclared deterministic WFS-base rule with ESTF release guard using laxity, queue age, priority/class deficit, service size, and bounded history slopes; no coefficient sweep
expected_runtime: <2 minutes local CPU; pure CSV/JSON analysis
failure_threshold: mean regret reduction <10% versus WFS, any favored-side safety regression >5%, quadrant ordering inverted, or >=90% overlap with old regime/static-index predictions
hypothesis: A WFS-safe deterministic composite scheduler rule with explicit ESTF completion-release guards can recover meaningful oracle headroom on TRAIN/D1 contested states without collapsing to the failed static analytic-index patterns.
name: family_a_mechanism_composite_rule_static_feasibility_v1
primary_metric: regret to certified ESTF/WFS pair envelope on TRAIN/D1 oracle rows
secondary_metrics: prediction collapse overlap with priority/regime identity

for_next_experiment: Stop if regret reduction versus WFS is <10%.
Stop if any favored side regresses versus WFS by >5%.
Stop if quadrant semantics are inverted or indistinguishable from the old analytic-index failure.
Stop if the rule overlaps regime identity/static priority by >=90%.
Stop if the only apparent gains depend on DEV/FINAL/TEST inspection or coefficient tuning.
stop_conditions.general: No D3/D4, no additional DAgger, no DEV-targeted bridge, no oracle acquisition, no selector retraining after WULVER_DEV_SUPPORT_NO_GO.

strict_stop_if_failure: If this static feasibility test fails, stop Family-A mechanism-derived scheduler synthesis unless a new non-selector mechanism is introduced outside the ESTF/WFS pair.
success_threshold: >=30% reduction in mean regret versus always-WFS on TRAIN/D1, no favored-side regret worse than WFS by >5%, correct quadrant ordering on contested events, and <80% prediction overlap with regime identity/static priority rule
